facts.claim: There was no effect for some outcomes such as attention and executive function for some noise sources such as road traffic noise and railway noise.

facts.claim: Aircraft noise effects on reading comprehension and on long-term memory were found to be of moderate quality.
facts.quote: the quality of the evidence across studies ranged from being of moderate quality for an effect for some outcomes, e.g. , aircraft noise effects on reading comprehension and on long-term memory

facts.claim: Indoor noise and reverberation in classroom settings is linked to poorer performance of children in verbal tasks.
facts.quote: Indoor noise and reverberation in classroom settings were found to be associated with poorer performance of the children in verbal tasks.

facts.claim: High exposure to aircraft noise is linked to lower reading performance.
facts.quote: Regarding chronic exposure to aircraft noise, studies consistently found that high exposure is associated with lower reading performance.

facts.claim: The evidence so far suggests that noise exposure is associated with cognition, but more good quality research using standardised methodology is required.
facts.quote: The evidence so far suggests that noise exposure is associated with cognition, but more good quality research using standardised methodology is required to corroborate these results

research.angle: While some evidence links specific noise sources like aircraft noise to lower reading performance, the quality of evidence varies significantly across different cognitive domains and noise types.
research.verdict: The evidence suggests a link between noise and cognitive performance in children, but results are inconsistent and often of low or moderate quality.
research.caveat: Many studies have low-quality evidence, lack standardized methodology, or fail to sufficiently control for confounding variables.
